Node and Python front doors disagree on 'add a changelog for this packet'
Option-line regex cannot match '1.' numbered lists

label: The ask-surface option-line regex has zero regression coverage: ask-surface-core.test.mjs returns no hits for OPTION_LINE, '1)' or '1.', so all three of its defects (the '1.' false negative, the '1)' false positive, and a single-digit ceiling that hides any list of ten or more) can be reintroduced or left unfixed with the suite still green.

The parity ratchet narrows rather than disappears: the CI drift-guard asserts the Python and TS routing maps both equal the registry projection, so map-level front-door divergence is reachable transitively, but outcome-level divergence (fusion, scoring, ordering) for one prompt has no gate and no suite.

The '181 hook adapters share one stdin module' sizing is not reproducible: a second independent measurement found 15 ask-surface-guard .cjs/.mjs files against the earlier pass's 200 hook sources / 40 stdin references, and neither basis yields 181. The substance holds; the number is unusable until its population is stated.

Advisor recommendation order is not explicable by any field the response returns: for 'add a changelog for this packet' the Node front door ranks sk-doc (score 0.347, confidence 0.82, uncertainty 0.20) above system-spec-kit (score 0.579, confidence 0.8313, uncertainty 0.16), so every visible axis favours the runner-up. Two executions at HEAD agree; whether this is a sort defect or an undocumented lane precedence is one read of the ordering function away, and it affects every recommendation the advisor returns.

The option-line regex's digit alternative is single-digit only, so a numbered list reaching ten items ('10)', '11)') matches neither branch: a third defect in OPTION_LINE that earlier passes did not record, on top of the '1.' false negative and the '1)' false positive.

Iteration 15 had already been recorded in the state log before re-dispatch, but with type/iteration/status/newInfoRatio/timestamp only: no runId, sessionId, lineageId, focus or answeredQuestions. Re-emitting through the append gateway with stable identity was required; receipt sequence 21 returned ok:true with projectionRefreshed:true.

The Python advisor front door could not be executed in this environment because the attempt was wrapped in 'timeout', which does not exist on this platform; the command failed before reaching Python. f-iter001-001's cross-door half therefore remains unexecuted and is not upgraded by this iteration.

direction: Inheriting the eight prior P1 verdicts without re-derivation
reason: All eight were treated as hypotheses and re-derived from HEAD. All eight reproduced; two were corrected in form (f-iter001-002 narrowed to outcome level; f-iter015-003's adapter count replaced, since neither pass's basis is reproducible), and one gained a third defect the earlier passes missed. The verdicts survive; the inherited numbers did not all survive.

direction: Calling the rank-1-below-runner-up ordering a sort bug
reason: A fused rank may legitimately weight a lane the response does not expose. The defensible, checkable claim is the narrower one: no field in the payload accounts for the ordering. Recording it as a finding with that scope rather than as a defect with an assumed mechanism.

label: The append gateway's state-log projection is lossy by exactly the fields the output contract marks required: a record carrying runId, sessionId, lineageId, focus and answeredQuestions was accepted and receipted (sequence 21, ok:true, projectionRefreshed:true), yet the refreshed deep-research-state.jsonl holds only type, iteration, run, status, newInfoRatio, ruledOut and timestamp. Refusal happens at the gateway boundary and the loss at the projection boundary, so the two never meet: the gateway has no reason to refuse and the log it writes is not schema-valid by its own contract. The failure mode is a re-dispatch loop rather than an error, which is consistent with this iteration arriving with its artifacts already on disk.

direction: Attributing the pre-existing malformed iteration-15 state-log record to a writer bypassing the gateway
reason: My own accepted append reproduced the identical reduced shape while carrying my newInfoRatio, proving the reduction is the gateway's own projection, not a bypass. Corrected in the narrative against my first reading.
